subject: Specifying Sub-questions in Lavaan Model Syntax

messages.author: d2b0929e2443470b
messages.subject: Specifying Sub-questions in Lavaan Model Syntax
parts:
Hello everyone,
 
I am trying to test the measurement invariance in my one-latent-factor model with CFA tests. I have 22 binary questions coded "correct" and "incorrect" and 3 different groups in my data. The sample sizes are approximately 200 for each group. Some of the questions are forms of sub-questions and some of these sub-questions are correlated since they are under the same questions. For example, Q11 consists of Q11A, Q11B, Q11C, and Q16 consists of Q16A, Q16B, and Q16C in the data. I have 4-5 questions in this form.

My question is how I should correctly specify this sub-questions concept in the model syntax. I couldn't find much information on the internet about sub-questions.

Here is the model when I treat all the sub-questions as one unique item for the latent factor.
model_mpck_fulldata <- 'MPCK =~ Q2B+Q4A+Q4B+Q7A+Q7B+Q11A+Q11B+Q11C+Q12A+Q14+Q16A+Q16B+Q16C+Q17B1+Q17B2+Q17B3+Q18A1+Q18A2+Q18A3+Q18A4+Q20B+Q21'
When I run this model, it doesn't even give good model fit results for the configural model (0.855 CFI and 0.843 TLI).  

I tried 2 different models which I get better results.
1-) If I specify the model like a second-order model below;
model_mpck_second_order <- ' Q11 =~ Q11A+Q11B+Q11C ; Q16 =~ Q16A+Q16B+Q16C; Q17B =~ Q17B1+Q17B2+Q17B3 ; Q18A =~ Q18A1+Q18A2+Q18A3+Q18A4 ;
MPCK =~ Q2B+Q4A+Q4B+Q7A+Q7B+Q11+Q12A+Q14+Q16+Q17B+Q18A+Q20B+Q21'
the model gives a lot better results (0.970 CFI and 0.966 TLI).

2-) I also tried to equalize some variance between some correlated sub-questions like in the model below;
model_mpck_combine_subquestions <- 'MPCK =~ Q2B+Q7B+Q7D+Q11A+Q11B+Q11C+Q12A+Q14+Q16A+Q16B+Q16C+Q17B1+Q17B3+Q17B4+Q18A1+Q18A2+Q18A3+Q20B+Q21;
Q16A~~Q16B; Q16A~~Q16C; Q16B~~Q16C; Q17B1~~Q17B3; Q17B1~~Q17B4; Q17B3~~Q17B4; Q18A2~~Q18A3'
and the results are even better (0.991 CFI, 0.990 TLI for configural and 0.955 CFI , 0.951 TLI for metric model).

Even if I did some research on the internet, I couldn't fully understand these models. Can I use one of these model concepts and which one makes more sense? Could anyone please assist me on this issue? Please forgive my ignorance if these 2 models make no sense at all. 

It would be very much appreciated if someone could make comments.
I wish everyone better model results and a productive day.
Best Wishes,
Enes.
